sections.label: PMA and National Monuments
sections.summary: Since the PMA was enacted in 1970, 73 National Monuments have been gazetted, given the highest legal protection among built heritage.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Since the PMA was enacted in 1970, we have gazetted 73 National Monuments, which are accorded the highest level of legal protection amongst all of our built heritage in Singapore.

sections.label: PMA monument definition expanded
sections.summary: The PMA will be amended to expand the definition of monument to include any site, including open spaces and inland water.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The PMA will, therefore, be amended to expand the definition of "monument" to include any "site", including open spaces and inland water, so that sites of national historical significance like the Padang can be preserved.

sections.label: New section 15(1A) approval
sections.summary: Under amendments in new proposed section 15(1A), new sets of actions on protected sites will require NHB's prior approval.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Under these amendments, which are set out in the new proposed section 15(1A), these new sets of actions will also require NHB's prior approval before they can be carried out on protected sites.

sections.label: Protection for NOI subjects
sections.summary: Amendments in clauses 6, 7 and 11 will extend protection to monuments or sites that are the subject of NOIs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The amendments, therefore, in clauses 6, 7 and 11 will extend protection to monuments or sites that are the subject of NOIs.

sections.label: NHB officers forcible entry
sections.summary: Amendments in clause 9 to section 27 will enable NHB officers who are public servants to forcibly enter any land or site without warrant.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Just as similar powers are accorded to competent authorities under the Planning Act, the amendments in clause 9 to section 27 of the Act will enable NHB officers who are public servants – namely, the Director of National Monuments or a Monument Inspector – to forcibly enter any land or site without warrant.

sections.label: Reasonable grounds suspicion
sections.summary: First, NHB must suspect on reasonable grounds that an offence under the PMA has been or is being committed in relation to the land or site.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: First, NHB must suspect on reasonable grounds that an offence under the PMA has been or is being committed in relation to the land or site.

sections.label: Powers to photograph and record
sections.summary: Amendments to section 27 let the Director or Monument Inspector take photographs or audio or video recordings within the land or site.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Taking reference from the Planning Act, the amendments to section 27 of this Act will also allow the Director or Monument Inspector to take photographs or make an audio or video recording within the land or site.

sections.label: Enforcement Notice for proposed monuments
sections.summary: Section 18 would be amended so NHB can serve an Enforcement Notice to stop activity risking a proposed National Monument.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We propose correspondingly to also extend this to a proposed National Monument as well.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Hence, on that score, we propose to amend section 18 of the Act so that NHB can serve an Enforcement Notice to put a stop to any operation or activity that may place a proposed National Monument at risk of being altered, removed, damaged or destroyed.

sections.label: Agency action and composition fines
sections.summary: Other public agencies can act, routine repair works are facilitated, and clauses 10 and 12(1) require NHB composition fines to go to the Consolidated Fund.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In those situations, those other public agencies will be able to take the appropriate action.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: These amendments will also facilitate routine repair and maintenance works, which would not alter or damage a National Monument.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Second, Madam, the amendments in clauses 10 and 12(1) of the Bill will require the payment of composition fines collected by NHB into the Consolidated Fund instead of retaining them.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: This is to give effect to a 2016 policy introduced by the Treasury, after the last set of amendments were made to the PMA.

sections.label: Protecting proposed National Monuments
sections.summary: The amendments seek to strengthen the PMA to safeguard key markers of national identity for future generations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: There must, therefore, also be sufficient measures in place to protect the character and integrity of future proposed National Monuments which are deemed worthy of preservation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: These amendments, therefore, seek to strengthen the provisions in the PMA to further safeguard key markers of our national identity, for future generations of Singaporeans.

sections.label: Leniency under new section 15
sections.summary: The new section 15 provides some leniency to those who damage or alter monuments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The new section 15 provides some leniency to those who damage or alter our monuments.

sections.label: Safety defence for section 15(4)
sections.summary: A person is not liable for a section 15(4) offence if he acted for safety and exercised all reasonable care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: A person will not be liable for a section 15(4) offence if he had acted because of a person’s or property’s safety and had exercised all reasonable care to ensure that the act or omission would have no more effect on the “character or appearance” of the monument than was “necessary in the circumstances”.

sections.label: Forced entry without warrant powers
sections.summary: New section 27 lets a Director or Monument Inspector forcibly enter land without warrant if conditions are met, though time sensitivity is not one of them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: With the new section 27, a Director or a Monument Inspector will have the power to forcibly enter any land or site without warrant if certain conditions are fulfilled.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I agree with the Director and Inspector having stronger enforcement powers and understand that there could be certain situations where taking enforcement action can be urgent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, I note that time sensitivity is not one of the conditions that have to be met for the Director or Inspector to enter the premises without a warrant.

sections.label: Monument Inspector forced entry concerns
sections.summary: Section 27(2A) lets a Monument Inspector forcibly enter a site without warrant on reasonable grounds of defacement, damage or interference, including breaking open doors or windows.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, I would like to talk about protecting the interests of owners and occupiers of actual and proposed national monuments through appropriate judicial oversight.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I note with particular concern that section 27(2A) will enable the Monument Inspector to “forcibly enter” the site “without warrant” when they suspect on reasonable grounds that the site is being defaced, damaged or interfered with, “including by breaking open any outer or inner door or window”.

sections.label: Proposed limits on forced entry
sections.summary: The speaker proposes limiting forced entry without warrant to non-compliance with a section 21 injunction or belief that irreparable damage will occur before an injunction is obtained.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The owner is compelled to comply with the injunction or may be charged with contempt of Court and possibly a jail term.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Hence, I propose to circumscribe the powers of forced entry without warrant to the following situations: firstly, non-compliance of the owner with an injunction issued under section 21; or, secondly, where there is reason to believe, on balance of probability considerations, that irreparable damage to the site will happen before an injunction order can be obtained.

sections.label: UK heritage forced entry warrant
sections.summary: The UK's Planning (Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) Act section 88 allows forced entry into recognised heritage sites only with a magistrate's warrant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The UK’s Planning (Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) Act, section 88, also allows for forced entry into recognised heritage sites, but only with a magistrate’s warrant.

sections.label: PMA dwelling-house preservation order
sections.summary: Section 12 of the PMA requires dwelling-houses served a preservation order to be acquired by the state within a year or the order lapses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And I seek assurances from the Minister on this point.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I note that section 12 of the PMA does require that dwelling-houses that are served a preservation order be acquired by the state within a year, or the preservation order would lapse.

sections.label: Proposed monument declaration rules
sections.summary: Section 2B limits a proposed monument declaration to 12 months, and section 2C lets owners or occupiers of private land apply for withdrawal, which the Authority must consider within one month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Section 2B of the Ordinance provides that the declaration of a “proposed monument” only has effect for 12 months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Section 2C of the Ordinance provides that if the proposed monument is within private land, the owner or occupier may at any time apply to the Authority for withdrawal of the declaration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Authority has to consider such objections within one month of the objection.

sections.label: Restoration and reconstruction difficulties
sections.summary: Restoration and reconstruction took almost 20 years due to difficulty finding local craftsmen with expertise and bringing in foreign craftsmen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the 1990s, it fell into disrepair and was infested by termites.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But the restoration and reconstruction took almost 20 years due to the difficulties in, firstly, finding local craftsmen with the necessary expertise and, secondly, bringing in foreign craftsmen.

sections.label: Statutory duty to consult
sections.summary: The speaker proposes statutory authorities be under a statutory obligation to consult the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and/or the NHB before acting on national monuments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To address this, I propose that statutory authorities be under a statutory obligation to consult the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and/or the NHB before taking or omitting to take any acts in relation to a national monument or proposed national monument.

sections.label: Mandatory heritage impact assessment scheme
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government to implement a mandatory heritage impact assessment scheme for development plans likely to impact heritage sites, enshrined in law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Next, Madam, going forward, I urge the Government to implement a mandatory heritage impact assessment (HIA) scheme for development plans that are likely to impact any heritage sites.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In an answer to a Parliamentary Question (PQ) I raised in February this year, MND explained that every development proposal is subject to a robust planning evaluation process that considers the development’s impact on traffic, public health, environment, as well as built heritage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to go one step further in enshrining this process in law and committing to a rigorous and transparent HIA process with deeper engagement with the public and civil society.

sections.label: 38 Oxley Road heritage due process
sections.summary: The Workers' Party has no position on 38 Oxley Road but cares about heritage due process being upheld rigorously, transparently and fairly, setting a precedent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Lastly, Mdm Deputy Speaker, one issue which I think looms large in the public mind and represents a potential conflict between the interests of the owner, occupier and heritage preservation mandate of the state is the status of 38 Oxley Road, the former home of our first Prime Minister, the late Mr Lee Kuan Yew.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Workers’ Party does not have a position on what should be done with the house and neither do we think it is our place to decide, but what we care deeply about is the heritage due process that we hope will be upheld, in a rigorous, transparent and fair manner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Given the high-profile nature of this case, how it is handled will set a precedent for future heritage decisions.

sections.label: Stronger safeguards and public consultation
sections.summary: The speaker calls for stronger safeguards on forced entry without warrant, greater certainty of timelines for monument owners, and deeper public consultations on monument preservation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On this note, Mdm Deputy Speaker, and, in conclusion, I call for stronger safeguards on the powers of forced entry without warrant, greater certainty of timelines for monument owners and deeper public consultations and engagement on monument preservation and conservation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This deep question goes to the heart of the tension between our economic or material aspirations and our cultural aspirations as a society.

sections.label: Conserved buildings and National Monuments
sections.summary: Today there are more than 7,000 conserved buildings under URA and 73 National Monuments under NHB.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Today, we have more than 7,000 conserved buildings under URA and 73 National Monuments under NHB.

sections.label: Monument enforcement and public education
sections.summary: The Minister said the Preservation of Monuments Act will align NHB's enforcement powers with the Planning Act, and a member asked about stronger legal protection and public education.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: The Minister said that the Preservation of Monuments Act will align NHB's powers of enforcement with those under the Planning Act for conserved buildings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: This is a good step, but I suggest that the Government look into whether there is a need to strengthen the legal protection of National Monuments beyond that which is accorded to conserved buildings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: In addition, I would like to ask about the efforts that NHB has undertaken, and will undertake, to educate the general public, particularly school children, on the significance of our National Monuments.

sections.label: Strengthening safeguards for built heritage
sections.summary: The Bill's amendments seek to strengthen identity and belonging by enhancing safeguards for built heritage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The amendments in this Bill seek to strengthen our sense of identity and belonging by enhancing the safeguards for our built heritage.

sections.label: Robust enforcement powers for monuments
sections.summary: The amendments take reference from the Planning Act to make enforcement powers robust as more places can be gazetted as National Monuments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The fundamental consideration is to ensure that the value and distinctive nature of these places, monuments, sites are well-preserved and protected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: These amendments will ensure that our enforcement powers can be sufficiently robust as we expand the range of what can be gazetted as National Monuments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: As I mentioned earlier, the proposed amendments we have in this Bill will take reference from the Planning Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: These powers in the Planning Act have worked well to protect the more than 7,000 conserved buildings, but, at present, do not extend to National Monuments.

sections.label: Entry and inspection powers abroad
sections.summary: Hong Kong allows officers to enter and inspect monuments with 48 hours' notice, and the UK allows authorised persons to enter land for surveying.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In Hong Kong, as Mr Leon Perera said, provided 48 hours' notice is given, the officer concerned may, at all reasonable times, enter and inspect any proposed monument or monuments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In the UK, section 88 of the Planning (Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) Act provides that any person duly authorised by the Secretary of State may at any reasonable time enter any land for the purposes of surveying any building on it, or any other land in connection with the proposal to include the building or exclude it from a list of works and so on.

sections.label: Plaques at National Monuments
sections.summary: A plaque already stands at a prominent area of each National Monument to inform the public of its status and significance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Mr Louis Ng suggested clear signs and labels around National Monuments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: He might be happy to know that, today, there is already a plaque at a prominent area at each of our National Monuments, such as at the entrance of the monument, to inform the public of the status of the property and also share its significance.

sections.label: Tours and monument learning programmes
sections.summary: Activities include public walking tours, school learning journeys led by volunteer guides, and the 2019 Milestones Through Monuments programme with onsite exhibits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: This includes walking tours for the public, learning journeys for school children, at least in pre-pandemic times, led by volunteer guides who share stories of the history and significance of the National Monuments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: There is also the Milestones Through Monuments programme, introduced in 2019, which allows the public to learn more about the history of each monument through onsite exhibits and physical installations.

sections.label: Music at Monuments digital programme
sections.summary: The Music at Monuments digital programme, online musical performances at National Monuments, was released last year and garnered over 300,000 views.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Other initiatives include the Music at Monuments digital programme, a series of musical performances held at National Monuments streamed online, which was released last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And I am pleased to say – perhaps because people cannot be physically present as much as they would like to be – that it garnered more than 300,000 views, which is very encouraging.

sections.label: Section 27 damage last resort
sections.summary: For NHB, any damage to a heritage site is an absolute last resort, only if necessary to protect the greater site itself.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I would just like to respond to some of the specific points that Mr Leon Perera raised, in terms of trying to strike a balance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I have explained how section 27 is designed to work, but Members will be assured to know that, as far as NHB is concerned, any damage to the heritage site will be an absolute last resort, only if necessary to have a protection of the greater site itself.

sections.label: NOI publication and public feedback
sections.summary: Anyone may make submissions and give feedback to NHB at any time, and once an NOI is filed it is published for the public.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: It does not stop anyone with any interest from making submissions and giving feedback to NHB at any time, which has happened.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, what the provisions do is to say that the moment something is considered and an NOI is filed in respect of that particular site or building, then that would be published and members of the public will know about it.

sections.label: Section 22A other agencies works
sections.summary: Section 22A lets other agencies deal with their works without running afoul of PMA, with close collaboration between MCCY, NHB and URA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: What section 22A does is to provide that these other agencies may come in and deal with their area of operations, their works, without running afoul of PMA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: To Mr Leon Perera's suggestion, he should be assured that there is close collaboration between MCCY and also with NHB, together with URA, whenever there are such works that concern or touch on or impact heritage sites or buildings.
